title: LPST protests: Keralam mulling lowering teacher-student ratio in govt schools with division fall leading to loss of post

ai.summary: Kerala government considers lowering teacher-student ratio to 1:25 in government schools where student numbers drop, to retain teachers from redeployment due to vacancies, but not for aided schools. Implementation may cost ₹50 crore annually.

facts.claim: Keralam government is mulling lowering the teacher-student ratio to 1:25 only in government schools where a fall in student strength leads to loss of teaching post
facts.quote: In a step towards ending the agitation in front of the Secretariat by All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers’ (LPST) Rankholders’ Association, the Keralam government is mulling lowering the teacher-student ratio to 1:25 only in government schools where a fall in student strength leads to loss of teaching post.

facts.claim: At present, the teacher-student ratio is 1:30 in lower primary schools
facts.quote: At present, the teacher-student ratio is 1:30 in lower primary schools.

facts.claim: The government is considering reducing this to 1:25 in government lower primary schools where there is a drop in the number of students in order to protect the teachers in that post itself
facts.quote: The government is considering reducing this to 1:25 in government lower primary schools where there is a drop in the number of students in order to protect the teachers in that post itself.

facts.claim: This in turn will help avoid redeployment of the teachers who are “thrown out” owing to division fall in vacancies arising owing to retirements every year
facts.quote: This in turn will help avoid redeployment of the teachers who are “thrown out” owing to division fall in vacancies arising owing to retirements every year.

facts.claim: With this, the retirement vacancies could be filled up from the current LPST rank-lists
facts.quote: With this, the retirement vacancies could be filled up from the current LPST rank-lists.

facts.claim: Another proposal under consideration is making appointments from LPST rank-lists to vacancies that arise from exempting head teachers from teaching duties in schools that have 150 or more students
facts.quote: Another proposal under consideration is making appointments from LPST rank-lists to vacancies that arise from exempting head teachers from teaching duties in schools that have 150 or more students.

facts.claim: At present, the head teacher vacancies (HTV) are filled by appointing teachers on daily wages
facts.quote: At present, the head teacher vacancies (HTV) are filled by appointing teachers on daily wages.

facts.claim: Both these proposals are likely to come up in Wednesday’s Cabinet meeting
facts.quote: Both these proposals are likely to come up in Wednesday’s Cabinet meeting.

facts.claim: Implementation of these two proposals is expected to create an additional financial burden of ₹50 crore a year
facts.quote: Implementation of these two proposals is expected to create an additional financial burden of ₹50 crore a year.

facts.claim: After the LPST rank-holders had intensified their over 130-day protest, saying they would not give up until their demands were met, the Chief Minister’s Office had signalled the intention for further discussions
facts.quote: After the LPST rank-holders had intensified their over 130-day protest, saying they would not give up until their demands were met, the Chief Minister’s Office had signalled the intention for further discussions.

facts.claim: The LPST rank-holders were demanding implementation of the 1:25 ratio across lower primary schools
facts.quote: The LPST rank-holders were demanding implementation of the 1:25 ratio across lower primary schools.

facts.claim: However, this would incur an additional expenditure of ₹400 crore, the Minister had pointed out
facts.quote: However, this would incur an additional expenditure of ₹400 crore, the Minister had pointed out.

facts.claim: The latest proposals are expected to assuage the striking rank-holders to an extent and resolve the current impasse
facts.quote: The latest proposals are expected to assuage the striking rank-holders to an extent and resolve the current impasse.

ai.background_note: Kerala government proposes to lower teacher-student ratio from 1:30 to 1:25 in government schools with declining student numbers to retain teachers, potentially reducing redeployment due to retirement vacancies, but not for aided schools.
